incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 — auth failures observed for tenant StalwartCorp in private VPC (dedicated-pool a3-prod). Pager triggered: high rate of token exchange failures and TLS handshake errors on ingress. Escalated to on-call. :rotating_light:
Maya (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing a spike of 502/401 from the auth bridge around 03:12 UTC. Affected routes: /v1/identity/exchange, /v1/serve/* (a3-prod).
Maya (oncall): Quick summary for folks joining: customer recently rotated OIDC keys last night. We started seeing errors at ~03:10 UTC.
Jordan (SRE): logs from edge-gateway show repeated errors: 
```
2026-03-15T03:12:08Z auth-bridge a3-prod ERROR validation failed: invalid_signature (kid="ek9nH...")
2026-03-15T03:12:09Z tls handshake failed: remote error: tls: handshake failure
```
Jordan (SRE): looks like our JWKS cache didn't pick up the new signing key. Also seeing mTLS failures for backend connection to dedicated pool nodes (x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid).
Leah (eng): Confirming: customer rotated id provider keys (Stalwart) at ~02:45 UTC. Our JWKS fetch TTL is normally 5m but there was a transient 429 from their jwks endpoint at 02:46, which prevented rotation from being observed. The bridge still has old keys pinned.
Alex (support): Sarah at Stalwart is on the channel: "we rotated keys this morning and started seeing errors when traffic increased around 03:00". Customer reports about 40% of token exchanges failing, user-facing auth timeouts. They've started a limited maintenance notice.
Sarah (StalwartCorp): thanks team. We're seeing failed sign-ins and API 401s across several services. Happy to coordinate.
Priya (SE): Can we do a temporary safe-accept policy: if signature validation fails for new tokens, fallback to previous key for 90s while we force-refresh JWKS? Need risk assessment first.
Jordan (SRE): Risk: accepting old KID could be abused if keys were intentionally revoked. But given customer rotation was planned (they confirmed), I think temporary fallback for a short window is acceptable. Alternative: force JWKS fetch and route traffic to regional fallback identity proxy.
Leah (eng): Steps I'm going to run now (control-plane):
```
# force-refresh tenant JWKS
tenantctl auth jwks refresh --tenant stalwart --force

# check bridge cache
kubectl -n tenant-stalwart logs deploy/auth-bridge -c bridge | tail -n 50 | grep JWKS
```
Leah (eng): running the refresh...
Leah (eng): refresh returned 200, new KID set: "pQ2rZ...". Bridge logs show successful update: 
```
2026-03-15T03:17:02Z auth-bridge INFO JWKS refreshed for tenant=stalwart, keys=3
```
Leah (eng): however, mTLS errors persist for dedicated-pool a3-prod when the bridge calls the worker nodes: 
```
x509: certificate has expired (notAfter=2026-03-15T00:00:00Z)
```
Maya (oncall): ah, dedicated pool node cert expired at midnight UTC. That explains TLS handshake failures. This is separate from JWKS but caused connection failures for some token exchanges.
Jordan (SRE): Mitigation plan: 1) Force JWKS refresh (done), 2) temporarily enable fallback KID acceptance for 60s if JWT validation fails, 3) rotate mTLS cert on a3-prod nodes (short window, momentum). I'll take cert rotation.
Alex (support): I've posted interim customer update: "We've identified two contributing issues: an OIDC key rotation that wasn't pulled due to a transient rate limit, and an expired mTLS cert on the dedicated pool. We're applying a staged mitigation now; traffic may be intermittently degraded for a short window. We'll update ASAP." :thumbsup:
Jordan (SRE): Rotating mTLS certs — running cert-rotate job for a3-prod nodes: 
```
# trigger rotation
infractl cert rotate --pool a3-prod --tenant stalwart --mode rolling

# watch
kubectl -n pools-a3 get pods -l pool=a3-prod -w
```
Jordan (SRE): rotation started. Rolling restarts, one node at a time. Monitoring handshake success metrics.
Leah (eng): I also pushed a quick fallback change to auth-bridge config to accept previous KID for 60s if the new KID validation fails: 
```
auth.bridge.jwt.validation.fallback_window=60s
```
Leah (eng): change applied via configmap; restarting auth-bridge pods now.
Maya (oncall): auth-bridge pods restarted, healthchecks green. Preliminary metrics: token exchange success rate improved from ~60% to ~95% within 4 minutes.
Sarah (StalwartCorp): saw immediate improvement, majority of users can sign in again. Thanks.
Priya (SE): Are we tracking exact customer-impacted time window and root cause? We should capture in the postmortem: JWKS fetch hit 429 then missed rotation + expired mTLS cert that wasn't auto-rotated.
Jordan (SRE): Agreed. I'll create an incident artifact and capture timeline. We should also add a preflight to control-plane to detect 4xx/5xx when fetching tenant JWKS and alert earlier.
Alex (support): Noting customer request: they'd like our confirmation that we will add a health-check and increase monitoring on tenant JWKS fetch failures. I've logged a follow-up with CSM.
Maya (oncall): Handoff: I'm handing pager to night shift @Jordan in 30 minutes. Current status: mitigated (traffic routing & fallback enabled); mTLS rotation in progress (nodes 1/5 rotated). Monitoring for 30m.
Jordan (SRE): taking the remainder of the shift. I've documented runbook steps in the incident doc: quick commands, rollback steps, and the safe-accept window we used.
Leah (eng): action items created: 
- runbook: add JWKS 429 detection and ticketing (owner: eng-runtime)
- infra: ensure cert auto-rotation for dedicated pools (owner: eng-infra)
- support: customer post-update & RCA timeline (owner: Alex)
Maya (oncall): final note for now: major customer impact window ~03:10–03:18 UTC. Root causes: brittle JWKS handling on transient 429 + expired pool cert. Mitigation: forced JWKS refresh + temporary KID fallback + rolling cert rotation.
Sarah (StalwartCorp): appreciate the quick response. Please keep us posted on RCA and when cert rotation completes.
Jordan (SRE): will follow up in incident doc and close after monitoring window. :white_check_mark:
